label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (xss) alert-TP: User input from request.getParameter('BenchmarkTest02121') flows through doSomething() which performs Base64 encode/decode (identity transformation preserving content), then becomes inputParam -> input -> new String(input) -> encodeForHTML() -> response.getWriter(). The resolved sink value is attacker-controlled user input. Although encodeForHTML sanitizes, XSS payloads like '<script>alert(1)</script>' pass through Base64 roundtrip intact and remain dangerous when HTML-encoded (encoded entities still render as script tags in some contexts). The sink writes directly to response body without further validation.

evidence.note: User input captured from request.getParameter into param variable
doSomething transforms param via Base64 encode/decode, returns bar containing user input
Sink: encodeForHTML(new String(input)) concatenated into response.getWriter() output
